standing: Independent OWNER/REFERENCE review of frozen 371 r3. Not acceptance, not five-field binding, not S9.3, not OS qualification.
requiredFindings: Ordinary-recovery still ACTIVEs a RESERVED row on complete-initial+exact marker. That filesystem shape is also the adoption interruption after fresh-N publication with a pre-existing bundle marker. Distinguishing those cannot be done from namespace/marker observations alone; the RESERVED row has no kind (random vs adopt). Ordinary recovery of complete-initial+exact would activate an adoption-shaped reservation without re-acquiring admitted-bundle context. r3 only refuses ordinary-recovery for absent-namespace+exact-marker, which is necessary but not sufficient.

r2RequiredFindings.adoptionCreateNewVsReconfirm: ADDRESSED in draft §Explicit adoption reservation and completion for the absent-namespace+exact-marker case and for create-new-after-namespace when marker absent.
r2RequiredFindings.ordinaryAbsentNsExactMarker: ADDRESSED: ordinary-recovery returns ADOPTION_CONTEXT_REQUIRED; unknown mode NO_COMPLETION_AUTHORITY; fault ordinary-bypasses-adoption-context detected.

proposedConcreteCorrection: Persist reservation kind (random vs adopt) on the RESERVED row, OR treat a RESERVED projectId that already appears on any historical row as adopt-shaped. Ordinary-recovery may ACTIVE only random/first-use reservations. Adopt-shaped RESERVED requires admitted-adoption for every completion, including complete-initial+exact. Do not infer adoption from a caller mode string.
